label: Prepare
title: Give your model a consistent input.
text: Normalize signals and compose transforms with explicit training behavior. Keep selected targets and masks aligned with the data.
code:
import keras
from helia_edge.layers.preprocessing import Normalization1D

signals = keras.ops.ones((2, 128, 1))
normalize = Normalization1D(mean=0., variance=4.)
inputs = normalize(signals)
note: A small tensor example. Select your Keras backend before importing.

label: Build
title: A model family. Your configuration.
text: Start with a configurable architecture, then make the input shape and output classes your own. Keep the parameters alongside the trained weights.
code:
import keras
from helia_edge.models import TcnModel, compact_tcn_params

params = compact_tcn_params(filters=8)
inputs = keras.Input(shape=(240, 14), batch_size=1)
model = TcnModel.model_from_params(
    inputs, params, num_classes=2
)
note: Constructs a model with fresh weights. Training data comes from your task.

label: Train
title: Keep your Keras training workflow.
text: Use compile() and fit() with the components your task needs. Add progress reporting or explore a specialized training objective.
code:
from helia_edge.callbacks import TQDMProgressBar

history = model.fit(
    train_x, train_y,
    validation_data=(validation_x, validation_y),
    callbacks=[TQDMProgressBar()],
    epochs=10, verbose=0,
)
note: Uses your compiled model and training/validation arrays.

label: Evaluate
title: Measure what matters to your task.
text: Inspect classification errors or signal reconstruction quality. Choose metrics for the meaning of your outputs, not just a single aggregate score.
code:
from helia_edge.metrics import Snr

metric = Snr()
metric.update_state(reference_signals, predicted_signals)
print(metric.result())
metric.reset_state()
note: SNR example for aligned reference and predicted signals.

label: Export
title: Take a measured step toward inference.
text: Export a supported TensorFlow-backed model to LiteRT, inspect its predictions and keep the settings with the artifact.
code:
from helia_edge.export import ExportSpec, export_model

spec = ExportSpec(precision="a8w8", io_dtype="int8",
                  mode="concrete")
result = export_model(model, spec,
                      calibration=representative_x.astype("float32"))
print(result.sha256)
note: Requires a trained TensorFlow-backed model and representative inputs.
